Title: Calling IGrainFactory.GetGrain<T>(pk) from constructor is a bad practice ?
Description: I'm doing some experiments with the Orleans.

I tried to find the answer but i could not...

Is it a bad idea reusing another grain gathered from the constructor like this ?

```csharp
public class MainGrain : Grain, IMainGrain
{
    private readonly IOtherGrain _otherGrain;

    public MainGrain(IGrainActivationContext context, IGrainFactory grainFactory) 
    {
        _otherGrain = grainFactory.GetGrain<IOtherGrain>(context.GrainIdentity.PrimaryKeyString);
    }

    public ValueTask<Item> GetCurrentValue() =>
        _otherGrain.GetItem();

   //others methods here
}
````

MainGrain stay in memory longer then IOtherGrain... (Calling GetCurrentValue() may call a already collected grain)
